picks.title: Oxford lets OpenAI train its AI models on Bodleian Library
picks.excerpt: Oxford University will let OpenAI train its models on Bodleian Library collections, as staff voice concerns over reputational risk of partnering with ChatGPT's maker. New library/archive AI-training deal (distinct from the Japan used-books and BookPact stories).
picks.rationale: Freshest, highest-credibility item: a named major library signing an AI-training deal is a new event, distinct from the CRL model-terms paper (09-20) and Japan used-books story (09-26).

picks.title: If AI imagines before we do, what is left for illustrators?
picks.excerpt: Illustrator Daniela Frongia on publishers using generative AI to produce early cover and design ideas before briefing illustrators, and what that does to the illustrator's role. Cover/illustration angle.
picks.rationale: Most design-relevant piece in the pool: how publishers now use gen-AI for cover concepts before briefing illustrators; different author and argument from the 09-14 Scheffler comment.

picks.title: AI가 쓴 소설 가려내기, 문학 경험보다 AI 사용 경험이 도움
picks.excerpt: Study: readers who had used AI were better at telling AI-written fiction from human fiction than well-read literature fans, but overall participants guessed the author at or below chance. OFF-LIST (Korean).
picks.rationale: Fresh research finding that bears directly on this month's AI-authorship accusation wave (Orelien, Falade), adding evidence rather than another accusation story.

picks.title: Google's New AI Voice Model Copies a Voice From 30 Seconds - Voice Over Talent Industry News
picks.excerpt: Google's new Gemini 3.8 speech models can clone a voice from a 30-second sample, but only after the voice owner records spoken consent. What it means for narrators and voice talent. OFF-LIST (narration-voices angle; Gemini TTS may also surface in other sections).
picks.rationale: New model release with a consent-gated cloning step, framed for audiobook narrators; actionable for audio production and new relative to the Storytel recaps and Spotify narration items.

picks.title: [단독] ‘AI 직격타’ 논픽션 불황에…교양 전문 출판사, 문학서 활로 모색
picks.excerpt: With nonfiction/general-interest sales hit hard by AI answer engines, Korean trade-nonfiction publishers are moving into literary fiction. Market effect of AI on publishing. OFF-LIST (Korean).
picks.rationale: Exclusive reporting on a concrete market shift, with publishers changing their lists because AI answer engines are eating nonfiction sales. Chosen over the Apex eden press release and lower-tier local items.
